q: According to Sec. 5, what form(s) can the Construction Manager take?
o: Only a partnership made up of architects and engineers
Only a sole proprietorship belonging to the Owner
An individual or a firm
Only a licensed corporation
n: Sec. 5 states plainly that the Construction Manager may be an individual or a firm. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5)

q: Whose functions does Sec. 2.1 fold into the CM's responsibilities?
o: The Project Feasibility Team
The Construction Supervision Group (CSG)
The Board of Architecture
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
n: Sec. 2.1 states that the CM's responsibilities include the functions of the Construction Supervision Group (CSG), referencing Doc. 204-A and the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 2.1)

q: In SPP 204-B Sec. 5.1, the abbreviation IAPOA expands to what?
o: International Alliance of Professional Organizations of Architects
Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
Integrated Association of Philippine Owners and Architects
Institute of Architects and Planners of Asia
n: IAPOA stands for the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects, of which the RLA acting as CM must be a member in good standing. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5.1)

q: If an Owner has already directly engaged a CSG and then separately hires an Architect as CM, how does Sec. 2.2 define the CM's relationship to that CSG?
o: The CM has no say over that CSG at all
The CM must dissolve the CSG and bring in a replacement under his own employ
The CM is permitted to oversee the CSG that the Owner hired directly
The CM must fold the CSG's functions into his own personal duties
n: Sec. 2.2 provides that the CM may hire the CSG to be under his employ, or may instead supervise a CSG that was hired directly by the Owner. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 2.2)

q: Sec. 6.1 describes Construction Management services as compensated how?
o: Solely via profit-sharing arrangements with the Contractor
Under a fixed, government-set flat rate regardless of project size
Bundled into the Architect's basic design fee at no extra cost
On a separate basis, since construction management falls outside the Architect's regular services
n: Sec. 6.1 states that since construction management is not part of the regular services of the Architect, the services rendered by the Architect as CM shall be separately compensated. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 6.1)

q: An Architect serving as CM takes over direct, hands-on command of a subcontractor's crew, to the point that a court might read it as the Architect stepping into the Contractor's own liability. Which section is put at risk here, and what Civil Code article does it invoke?
o: Sec. 4.1, invoking Article 1159 of the Civil Code
Sec. 3.2, invoking Article 1900 of the Civil Code
Sec. 5.1, invoking Article 1723 of the Civil Code
Sec. 3.1, invoking Article 1723 of the Civil Code
n: Sec. 3.1 prohibits the CM from involving himself directly with the Contractor's work such that it may be construed that he is assuming the Contractor's liability, citing Article 1723, etc. of the Civil Code. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 3.1)

q: The 2010 SPP Document 204-B took the place of which older document?
o: 1979 UAP Doc. 205
1979 UAP Doc. 204-A
1979 UAP Doc. 204-B
2000 SPP Document 204
n: The heading of SPP Document 204-B explicitly states it is "replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 204-B." (Source: SPP Document 204-B, heading)

q: Sec. 4.1 makes the Architect-as-CM directly answerable to whom, and over which aspects of the work?
o: IAPOA, for professional discipline
The Building Official, for code compliance
The Contractor, for site safety
The Owner, for cost, quality and time control
n: Sec. 4.1 states the Architect as CM is directly responsible to the Owner on all aspects of the construction work: programming, coordination, quality and cost control, and time management. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 4.1)

q: Sec. 1.2 sets out the complete list of capacities in which a CM can serve. Which option matches that full list?
o: A government housing official or a member of the Owner's staff, but never an independent individual
A firm hired by the Contractor exclusively
A government-accredited engineer, a subcontractor, or the project's structural engineer
A member of the Owner's staff, an independent individual, or a firm the Owner hires
n: Sec. 1.2 lists three capacities: a member of the staff of the Owner, an independent individual, or a firm hired by the Owner to manage construction of a particular project. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.2.1-1.2.3)

q: When equipment malfunctions because of a flaw in how the work was built (not in the design), Sec. 4.2.2 clears the CM of liability under what condition?
o: Only when the Contractor admits fault in writing
The CM remains liable regardless, since construction method is his direct concern
As long as the CM properly performed his functions during construction/project implementation
Only if the malfunction happens within the construction's first month
n: Sec. 4.2.2 states the CM assumes no liability for equipment failure or collapse due to deficiencies in the manner of construction, provided the CM faithfully discharged his function/s during the construction/project implementation. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 4.2.2)

q: What, per Sec. 1.3, makes an Architect qualified to take on the Construction Manager role?
o: A separate PRC CM license
Ten years with one contractor
Training across specialties to coordinate work
An IAPOA CM certification course
n: Sec. 1.3 states that the Architect's training in various specialties allows him to serve as CM and supervise and assure proper coordination of all construction activities with regard to quality, workmanship and cost. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.3)

q: Besides being a state-regulated professional, what does Sec. 5.1 require of the individual CM (or the principal of a firm serving as CM)?
o: A CM graduate with no license
Any bonded licensed professional
A civil engineer with a PCAB license
An experienced RLA with a current ID, IAPOA member
n: Sec. 5.1 requires the individual/principal to preferably be an Architect with managerial capabilities and extensive experience in construction, a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) with an updated professional identification card, and a member in good standing of IAPOA. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5.1)

q: Sec. 2.1.1 through 2.1.4 lists four CM functions. Which of these is not one of them?
o: Detailed architectural design
Quality control of work
Keeping of records
Coordination and supervision
n: The four listed CM/CSG functions are Coordination and Supervision, Cost and Time Control, Quality Control of Work, and Keeping of Records. Preparing the detailed architectural design is a regular design service, not a CM function. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 2.1.1-2.1.4)

q: Sec. 5.2 describes which architects as generally well-suited to become Construction Managers?
o: Architects new to contractors
Recently licensed graduates
Architects who contract or have run construction
Government-employed architects only
n: Sec. 5.2 states that Architects who are Contractors, or who have already been in responsible charge of construction works, are usually capable of becoming CMs. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 5.2)

q: Sec. 3 restricts the Architect-as-CM from doing which of these?
o: Keeping cost and time records
Coordinating with the Owner
Receiving separate CM compensation
Taking over or disrupting the contractor's work
n: Sec. 3.1 and 3.2 set the two limitations on the CM's authority: not assuming the Contractor's liability, and not imposing methods/systems/designs that substantially affect the schedule and impair the design concept. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 3.1-3.2)

q: What does SPP Document 204-B chiefly address, and under what legal authority is it issued?
o: Design-build services, under the National Building Code
Construction Supervision Group services, as a standalone SPP unconnected to any statute
Project feasibility studies, as part of the IRR of R.A. No. 545
Construction Management Services, forming part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266
n: SPP Document 204-B covers Construction Management Services and forms part of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of R.A. No. 9266, the Architecture Act of the Philippines. (Source: SPP Document 204-B, title/heading)

q: Acting as CM, an Architect single-handedly rolls out a new construction method that meaningfully shifts the schedule and reshapes his own design concept. Does Sec. 3.2 permit this?
o: Yes — the CM controls all methods
Yes — if the Owner is not told
No — only without prior design approval
No — that is barred by Sec. 3.2
n: Sec. 3.2 explicitly limits the CM from imposing methods, systems, or designs that will substantially affect the construction schedule and impair the design concept of the Architect. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 3.2)

q: What development, per Sec. 1.1, prompted the creation of Construction Management Services?
o: A law requiring a CM above a set cost
A shortage of licensed supervisors
The phase-out of the CSG system
Growing complexity and need for cost control
n: Sec. 1.1 states that due to the increasing complexity of construction projects, there is an upward demand for more effective cost control and faster project implementation consistent with high quality of work, which Construction Management Services were instituted to address. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.1)

q: When part of a structure collapses because of a design flaw, under what condition does Sec. 4.2.1 excuse the CM from liability?
o: The CM is never liable for such deficiencies under any circumstance
Only when the CM also happens to be the original design architect
As long as the CM took no part in reviewing and approving the plan/design
In every case, regardless of the CM's role in reviewing the design
n: Sec. 4.2.1 provides that the CM assumes no liability for collapse due to deficiencies in the plan/design, provided the CM did not participate in the plan/design review and approval. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 4.2.1)

q: An Owner wants to designate an in-house, salaried staff member as CM rather than hiring an outsider. Does SPP 204-B permit this?
o: No, an independent third party is always required
Yes, but only if that staff member also happens to be the project's Contractor
No, only a firm may serve as CM, never an individual staff member
Yes — Sec. 1.2.1 specifically permits the CM to be drawn from the Owner's own staff
n: One of the three recognized capacities for a CM under Sec. 1.2.1 is being a member of the staff of the Owner, so this arrangement is permitted. (Source: SPP 204-B, Sec. 1.2.1)
